title: The Sky of Paper Stars
story:
The sixty-second morning of James's journey broke under a sky so clear and bright it felt polished by the highland wind. Leaving the quiet shelter of his cedar shelf in the old shed, James stepped into the carpentry yard to find Don Tadeo surrounded by vibrant rolls of thin tissue paper and long, flexible splints of bamboo. The air in Aldea San Gabriel was electric with quiet industry. Doors stood open all down the cobblestone lane, and children darted past carrying bundled wooden frames decorated with yellow, turquoise, and magenta streamers.

James watched the orange paper catch the early light. He watched the crimson paper flutter like butterfly wings against the dusty ground. He watched the old carpenter tie swift, practiced knots of cotton twine, binding two thin bamboo ribs into a neat cross before wrapping a vibrant star of paper around its frame. Without a word, the man motioned for James to hold the edge of the paper taut, inviting his small hands into the rhythm of the work.

By mid-morning, the entire village seemed to migrate up the winding dirt path toward the windy knoll overlooking the quiet adobe roofs and the distant peak of Cloudveil Ridge. It was the first day of November, and the sky above the hills was transformed into a soaring gallery of giant paper kites. Some were as wide as houses, octagonal stars of intricate cut paper that hummed and thrummed in the mountain thermal currents like living instruments.

Standing beside Don Tadeo amidst the laughing crowd, James lifted his smooth green sea-glass to his eye. Through the tinted lens, the fluttering sky blazed in shimmering shades of emerald and sapphire. Don Tadeo handed James a small carved wooden spool wound with sturdy twine, connected directly to the small star-shaped paper kite they had assembled together in the yard.

James took a cautious step forward, let out a few arm-lengths of string, and felt the breeze catch the paper star. With a sudden, buoyant tug, the little kite leaped into the blue, dancing gracefully above the cracked red tiles of his new home town.
location: The Windy Knoll above Aldea San Gabriel
